scope: All 23 *_test.go files under experiments/rust-process-owner/ffi/go, read in full; production Go review owned by root

findings.severity: medium for evidence claims; no production failure established
findings.condition: An ordinary test relies on own() teardown and Finish returns err=nil with Outcome.State=cleanupFailed; no earlier body assertion requires complete. Example: TestCheckedAdmissionNilPolicyDoesNotConsumeAdmission ends at admission_windows_test.go:158.
findings.behavior: own() explicitly accepts both complete and cleanupFailed, releases the allocation, and does not t.Error the unexpected cleanup failure. Library.Close can then succeed although failed native handle close remains recorded in Outcome.
findings.consequence: A PASS from such a test does not establish successful native cleanup. The cleanupFailed state is intentionally expected in native fault tests, so removing it globally would break their deliberate contract.
findings.minimal_next_action: If a change is later authorized, make ordinary teardown require complete and keep an explicit expected-cleanup-failure helper for fault cases. Preserve historical native outcomes. No new test or production edit performed.

findings.classification: confirmed static coverage limit supporting root candidate
findings.severity: conditional production cleanup error remains unqualified
findings.condition: bridge_open successfully loads a DLL, later fails required-export/version validation, then FreeLibrary fails.
findings.behavior: The tests cover successful failed-open cleanup via real module map/reference checks but never force the unload call itself to fail. faults_windows_test.go only substitutes producer fields and does not cover this.
findings.consequence: These tests do not refute the root-reviewed candidate that bridge_open fail-label ignores FreeLibrary return and frees its carrier, losing conditional cleanup failure/custody. This review has not induced that condition or verified a native occurrence.
findings.minimal_next_action: Keep candidate conditional and distinguish it from real protected CloseHandle qualification. Do not mark actual unload-error behavior covered.

findings.severity: low; failure-path bound depends on outer process owner
findings.condition: The 3-second EOF timer fires and endpoint Close or the worker fails to finish.
findings.behavior: Timeout branch executes endpoint Close then a bare receive from done with no remaining deadline.
findings.consequence: The per-test watchdog does not guarantee bounded cleanup; outer go test/process deadline remains the eventual guard. No hang was executed or observed in this review.
findings.minimal_next_action: Do not count the 3-second local timer alone as proof of bounded reader completion. Any eventual repair should retain the same reader and endpoint, preserve timeout status and avoid a new unrelated completion observer.

cross_cutting_limits: Source-defined cases are not executed-case counts. Tagged variants require exact recorded DLL/source provenance.
Metadata, identity token query/close and members transport faults are mostly separately built producer substitutions; do not promote them to real Windows API failures.

The native_cleanup and stdio protected-close tests are written to induce actual CloseHandle refusal on exact protected original/temporary handles, with explicit fixture recovery. They do not cover FreeLibrary.
memberFixture cleanup at members_windows_test.go:28-39 checks finalization but omits error/CleanupComplete; explicit requireMemberClose at lines 72–82 checks both and ordinary bodies mostly use it.
Several tests use background observation or WaitGroup joins that rely on finite fixtures/outer watchdog. This review makes no new claim of bounded whole-process completion.
No private binary SID/account markers were opened or printed.
No new native test, repeat 21-run qualification, production edit, publication or PR change was performed for this static review.
